chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'He has succeeded who purifies himself, and mentions the name of his Lord and prays.' He said: 'He goes to the prayer place and prays.'

key_terms.فَصَلَّى: And prayed (referring to the ritual prayer action)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'He has succeeded who purifies himself' in Surah Al-A'la according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* offers a concise exegetical breakdown of Surah Al-A'la (87:14-15), linking the verse's command to purify oneself with the physical act of performing ablution and proceeding to the prayer space (*jabbanah*). It further clarifies that 'mentioning the name of his Lord' corresponds to the *Takbir* and 'praying' to the *Salat* itself, establishing a direct correlation between spiritual purification and ritual action. This interpretation is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the sequential components of the prayer ritual as derived directly from the Quranic text.
